# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 35 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 1 — The Two Angels

**1** "In the first commandment," he said, "I directed you to guard faith and fear and self-control." "Yes, sir," I replied. **2** "Now I want to show you the powers of these, so that you may understand what each is and how it operates. **3** Their powers are twofold, and they relate equally to the righteous and the unrighteous." **4** "How so, sir?" "Listen," he said. "The righteous person has faith and fear and self-control. Now among the righteous there dwell two angels — one of righteousness and one of wickedness." **5** "But how will I know their workings, sir, since both dwell with me?" **6** "Listen and understand," he replied. "The angel of righteousness is gentle, modest, peaceful, and sensitive. When this one enters your heart, immediately it speaks to you of righteousness, of purity, of holiness, of contentment, of every righteous deed, and of every glorious virtue. When all these things arise in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. **7** These are the works of the angel of righteousness. Trust him and his works. **8** Now consider the works of the angel of wickedness. He is bitter, wrathful, and senseless, and his works are evil, casting down the servants of God. Whenever this one enters your heart, recognize him by his works. **9** He stirs up in you anger and bitterness and folly and every kind of wickedness. When these things arise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is within you. Knowing his works, keep away from him and trust him in nothing."

---

### Council Notes

Mandate 6 introduces the Two Angels doctrine — one of the most significant angelological teachings in the early Christian period. Its closest parallel is the Two Spirits of the Community Rule (1QS 3:13-4:26), suggesting a shared Jewish apocalyptic tradition.

The doctrine is practical and diagnostic: the two angels are identified not by vision or name but by the inner states they produce:
- **Angel of righteousness:** righteousness, purity, holiness, contentment, glorious virtues
- **Angel of wickedness:** anger, bitterness, folly, wickedness

The adjectives applied to the two angels are revealing:
- Righteous angel: gentle (hapalos), modest (tapeinophron), peaceful (hēsuchos), sensitive (praos)
- Wicked angel: bitter (pikros), wrathful (oxucholos), senseless (aphron), evil (ponēros)

The echo of Mandate 5's Holy Spirit language is intentional: the angel of righteousness shares the Holy Spirit's qualities of gentleness and sensitivity — suggesting they work together.
